title: Peeling off digits
summary: Use % 10 and / 10 to recurse on a number one digit at a time.

say.never: To work with the digits of a number: `% 10` gives you the **last digit**, and `/ 10` gives you **everything before it** (whole-number division throws the leftover away). So `472 % 10` is `2` and `472 / 10` is `47`.
say.bit: `% 10` is the last digit and `/ 10` is the rest.

board.code:
472 % 10   is 2    the last digit
472 / 10   is 47   everything before it
47 / 10    is 4
4 / 10     is 0

say.never: Counting the digits of 472 is 1 plus counting the digits of 47. Each call peels off one digit and hands the rest to a smaller call. When only one digit is left (any number under 10), you can answer straight away: that's the base case.
say.bit: Each call peels off one digit; a number under 10 is the base case.

marks.label: one digit left: the base case

steps.title: In your lesson: Splitting a number

say.never: `sumDigits` works the same way, but instead of adding 1 for each digit, add **the digit itself**. Use the three questions: the smallest input is one digit, and its sum is just itself. The smaller version is `n / 10`. To finish, add the last digit, `n % 10`.
say.bit: Same shape as `digitCount`, but add the digit (`n % 10`) instead of 1.
